r an account, and is what the command above uses.
## What it is

Ponytail by Dietrich Gebert, MIT licensed. It is one instruction
prompt plus a handful of one-shot c

ommand prompts; everything else in that repository is plumbing that loads the
prompt into a particul

ar agent. This bundle ships the prompt into DeepSeek Harness as a **skill** and as a
**system-prompt
section**, so it is present in every session without anyone installing a plugin.
Upstream is the source of truth for the rules. This bundle vendors **upstream ponytail 5.1.0** with

the review,
audit and ledger procedures folded in from the three upstream command skills, and
`scrip
ts/check-plugin.mjs` pins the same ten rule invariants upstream's own `scripts/check-rule-copies.js`
pins — so a silent upstream rule change cannot pass unnoticed.
## Why a skill and not an AGENTS.md file
`dsh-agent-instructions` already loads `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md` into every session, and a compact copy of

the rules
there would work. Three things make the skill the better home:
- **It is loadable on demand.** A `user-agents` copy at rank 500 competes with the per-project file;

a runtime
registration at rank 250 lets a project's own `ponytail` skill override it, which is the

behaviour a user
editing one repository expects.
- **It carries a description that routes it.** The

catalog shows the description to the model before it loads
anything, so the model knows when the mod

e applies instead of seeing an unconditional block of rules.
- **It is inspectable and editable.** `

assets/ponytail/SKILL.md` is one file a maintainer can read and edit;
editing it changes what the ne

xt session sees after a plugin reload. (The prompt section is not generated from
it — the section is
deliberately short, and carries the level rather than the rules.)
## What it gives a model
A `ponytail` skill and a `ponytail` system-prompt section. The section states the active level, what

the level
changes, and the two lines every reply owes the user. The skill body is the full ruleset
with the level tables.
## Levels
| Level | Behaviour |

| `lite` | Build what was asked, name the smaller option in one line |
| `full` | The complete rules

et (default) |
| `ultra` | Also question the request before building |
The default for **new sessions** is `cordis.patch.yml`'s `ponytail-runtime.config.defaultLevel`. A s

ession that
changes level keeps that level for the rest of the session, which is what upstream's ses

sion-scoped mode does.
Changing the default for new sessions is a patch-file edit, not a live Settin

gs row: this bundle ships a plain
Standard Schema config, and only a native Schemastery schema rende

rs a Settings form. A plugin must not import
`@deepseek-ai/schemastery` itself, so the row reports `
unsupported` rather than failing the load.
## Commands
| Command | What it does |
| `/ponytail [lite\|full\|ultra\|off]` | Set the level for this session, or report it with no argume

nt |
| `/ponytail-review` | Review the current change: bugs, security, load, missing tests, speed, w

hat to cut |
| `/ponytail-audit` | The same review for the whole repository, ranked |
| `/ponytail-d

ebt` | Harvest `shortcut:` comments into a ledger |
| `/ponytail-gain` | The measured-impact scorebo

ard |
| `/ponytail-help` | Quick reference card |

## Enabling it in a profile
The plugin is a bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and the profile lists it in both
`dependencies` and `dsh.profile.bundles`. `dsh plugin add` does both edits for you.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A checkout can be linked instead, with the bundle name and the directory left as whatever they are:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart DSH once** before it resolves. Editing `package.json` while DSH is running does not m

ake the bundle
resolvable: `dsh-app-boot`'s `resolveBundleDir` probes the `node_modules` lookup orde

r from the installation
anchor and the profile directory, and a running host holds the profile manif

est it read at launch. Until the link
exists, adding the bundle produces exactly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That install command materialises the link; the restart makes the running host read the new manifest

. Do both,
then hard-refresh the browser (`Ctrl + Shift + R`).
To turn the mode off without removing the bundle, set `defaultLevel: off` in the `ponytail-runtime`

row's config —
the skill, the section and the commands stay mounted, and the rules become available

on demand through the `skill`
tool.
